Thank you very much, Co-Chairs, Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen.

It is my great pleasure to deliver these closing remarks on behalf of the co-facilitators, Mexico, Nepal, Norway, and Zambia, at the conclusion of what has been a truly productive second session of the Preparatory Committee for the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development. As we move beyond the stock-taking phase initiated in Addis Ababa, we find ourselves at a pivotal moment. The time has come to transform our reflections into tangible commitments that will catalyze meaningful change. First and foremost, I extend our sincere gratitude to all of you, to all member states and stakeholders for their invaluable contributions, the insights shared through national statements, interactive dialogues and side over the past few days have underscored our collective dedication to the success of this process. We deeply appreciate the thoughtful engagement with the elements paper, as well as your constructive feedback, which has provided invaluable guidance for refining the document, for ensuring that it captures our shared aspirations while remaining grounded in actionable and pragmatic measures. In this context, I should emphasize that we have worked tirelessly to provide a document, an elements paper, that strikes a careful balance. It is designed to reflect the priorities of countries of varying and diverse contexts, ensuring that every one of you feels heard and represented. As we advance, we will thoroughly review all insights and contributions shared during this session. We encourage Member States and stakeholders to sustain their active engagement in the road ahead. By deepening consensus on widely supported proposals and bridging differences where they persist, we can ensure that the document reflects diverse perspectives. And we, the co-facilitators, remain fully committed to inclusive dialogue. This is not merely an open door policy. It is a genuine effort to listen, to adapt and build consensus around shared goals. We will be following up and reaching out with each and every one of you to continue listening and understanding your needs, your priorities, your sensitivities. This is the only way in which we, as co-facilitators, believe we can navigate the challenges before us and drive effective implementation of our shared aspirations through collaborative and ambitious efforts. We are receptive to all contributions, whether from Member States, civil society, academia or the private sector. because we believe that only by embracing this diversity can we generate a document that works for everyone. Our aim is to deliver an outcome document that balances ambition with practicality, aligns with today's realities, which are quite complex, and sets a clear path towards where we need to go. In doing so, we reaffirm our commitment to fostering solutions that are not only forward-looking, but also grounded in the voices and the aspirations of all. Looking ahead, I am pleased to announce that the zero draft will be circulated to member states and stakeholders on the week of January 17th. and that we plan to hold a one-day session to present the zero draft to all of you in the week of January 22nd before the third session of the preparatory committee, which is scheduled for February 10 to 14, which will now be hosted in New York and where Mexico will contribute towards its organization. We kindly remind participants to submit your written statements to both eStatements and to ffd4@un.org, including the subject line, the name of your country, and the relevant session details. Excellencies, now is the time for all of us to be together and be united. North and South must work together and find common ground and areas of synergy. And as we move ahead towards a successful FFD4 conference in Sevilla, let us not forget the purpose of our mission. to support countries in addressing existing inequalities, with the overarching focus on eradicating poverty through enhanced access to trade, better conditions to address their external debt crisis, strengthening domestic resource mobilization, and taking advantage of new and innovative finance mechanisms and digital financial technologies. We heard you, and we will continue to do so. Let me conclude by reaffirming our steadfast commitment to delivering a focused and actionable outcome document. We are fully aware of the complexities that multilateralism entails. the diversity of perspectives, the balancing of priorities, and the weight of expectations. But we are equally certain that it is the only path capable of delivering the profound and the transformative changes our world urgently needs. Only through collective action can we respond at scale to today's challenges and shape an international financial landscape that is fit for purpose, people-centered, and reflective of the current global configuration. Multilateralism empowers us to align diverse needs, drive sustainable progress, and confront the crisis of our time with unity and resolve, ensuring that no one is left behind. Let us forge ahead, keeping in mind the need for concrete short-term actions that can lead to long-term impactful reforms that set an ambitious, innovative, and inclusive financing agenda to fulfill the commitments of the Addis Ababa Action Agenda and to guide us in the right direction as we look to 2030 and beyond in a sustainable manner. Please, Excellencies, find in your FFD4 co-facilitators strong and committed partners in our journey together to achieve this collective goal of leaving no one behind. Thank you to all of you for your dedication, for your invaluable contributions, and we hope that you take advantage of the holiday break to rest and come back fully ready to engage in 2025. I thank you very much.
